title: 3 April 1973. The first handheld mobile call was made from a Manhattan pavement.
description:
The first handheld mobile call was made from a Manhattan pavement. Martin Cooper of Motorola stood on Sixth Avenue near the Hilton and rang Joel Engel, a rival at AT&T.

The phone only worked through one base station. Motorola's base station sat on the roof of Burlington House and was hardwired to the AT&T landline network.

The recharge time for about 30 minutes of talk. Cooper joked that you could not hold the phone up for that long.

Customers waited about ten years. Motorola unveiled the DynaTAC 8000X on 6 March 1983. Quantity production began in early April 1984.

The first commercial handset cost US$3,995 in 1984. Motorola's own forecast in 1973 had been full operation within three years.

His first call went to his chief competitor.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Cooper_(inventor): read. Established that Cooper made the first handheld cellular call on 3 April 1973 near the Hilton on Sixth Avenue in Manhattan; that the person called was Joel S. Engel, his chief competitor at AT&T; that the handset gave about 30 minutes of talk time before a 10-hour recharge; Cooper's remark that battery life was not really a problem because you could not hold the phone up for that long; and that bringing it to market took about 10 years.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorola_DynaTAC: read. Established that the call went through a Motorola base station on the roof of Burlington House hardwired to the AT&T landline network; that the DynaTAC 8000X was unveiled on 6 March 1983; that quantity production began in early April 1984 and it was priced at US$3,995 in 1984; that its lead gives a roughly 10-hour charge and 30 minutes of talk time; and that Motorola's 1973 forecast was for full operation within three years.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_phone: read (first part of the page). Established that the first handheld mobile phone call took place in New York City on 3 April 1973 and that the call was to a rival at AT&T.
